chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqoub ibn Salim, raising it (to the Imam), said:
Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not accumulate the dust behind the door, for it is a shelter of the Satans.'
ai.seo_question: Why is dust behind the door considered a shelter for devils in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) links the physical neglect of dust behind doors to spiritual vulnerability, identifying it as a dwelling place for devils. This hadith reflects the Shia emphasis on *taharat* (purity) extending beyond ritual ablution to include the domestic environment, where orderliness facilitates spiritual presence and wards off *shayatin*. The teaching underscores the holistic Islamic view that physical cleanliness is intrinsically tied to the state of the soul and its protection from evil influences.
